summary: Entera Bio reported Q1 2020 financial results with a net loss of $2.9 million and cash of $13.3 million, expecting to fund operations into Q2 2021. The company plans to study higher doses within current 2020 spend and expects six-month BMD data in Q3 2020, with Phase 3 targeted for late 2021 or 2022. COVID-19 caused moderate enrollment delays, but operations are resuming.

summary: For Q2 FY2020, Salarius Pharmaceuticals reported a net loss of $1.8 million ($0.13 per share), wider than the prior-year loss of $0.9 million ($0.30 per share) due to higher R&D and G&A costs. Cash stood at $7.2 million at quarter-end, supplemented by a $6.2 million offering in August and up to $9.1 million in grant funding, extending runway to late 2021. Early seclidemstat data show dose-proportional plasma levels and a reduction in target lesions in one patient, though RECIST classified the patient as progressive disease. The company plans to expand its Ewing sarcoma trial to include Ewing-related sarcomas, increasing expansion cohort from 20 to 50 patients, with early data expected in the second half of 2021.

summary: Entera Bio reported interim six-month data from the Phase 2 trial of EB613, showing a placebo-adjusted 2.15% increase in lumbar spine BMD at the 1.5 mg dose (p=0.08) and a significant dose-dependent trend across all doses. The company added a higher 2.5 mg dose group and discontinued lower doses, aiming to start a Phase 3 trial in late 2021 or 2022. H1 2020 revenue was $94,000 from the Amgen collaboration, with total operating expenses of $6.4 million and cash sufficient into Q2 2021. Enrollment was back on track with 131 subjects, and no serious drug-related adverse events were reported.

summary: Entera Bio completed enrollment of its Phase 2 EB613 trial with 161 patients despite COVID-19. The company expects final biomarker data including the new 2.5 mg dose in Q1 2021 and final BMD data in Q2 2021. Cash of $7.1 million at September 30, 2020 is expected to fund operations into Q2 2021, with an anticipated 2020 operating loss of approximately $11 million.

Management expects readouts around end of Q4 2021 or Q1 2022 and plans multiple new trials by mid-2021.

positive_highlights: Wavelo revenue up 174% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of $4.2 million, its strongest quarter since launch

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 13% year-over-year, partly due to currency effects.
Q4 2023 expected to be negatively impacted by the Israel-Hamas war.
Slow-moving inventory discounts reduced average note price to $4.35 per gram.
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 22% from 20% year-over-year.

Operating expenses reduced by 34% year-over-year.
summary: In Q3 2023, IM Cannabis reported revenues of $12.4 million, down 13% from $14.2 million in Q3 2022, with 6.4% of the decline attributed to unfavorable currency effects. Operating expenses fell 34% year-over-year, but the company faced headwinds from slow-moving inventory discounts, a delivery transition, and the onset of the Israel-Hamas war, which is expected to negatively impact Q4. Management remains focused on sustainable profitability and anticipates regulatory changes in Germany and Israel, but notes delays due to the war.

Pivotal trial costs estimated at $18M (AML) with no guarantee of external funding

summary: Moleculin reported preliminary Phase 2 data for Annamycin in AML and STS, showing a 38% complete response rate in heavily pre-treated AML patients and a 78% response rate with 56% 3-month PFS in STS at the optimal dose. Management is planning end-of-Phase 2 meetings with FDA/EMA and expects to start pivotal trials in 2024, with potential external funding for the STS pivotal trial.

summary: Moleculin Biotech reported clinical data from its Annamycin program in relapsed/refractory AML, with a 60% CRc rate (50% CR, 10% CRi) in second-line patients from the MB-106 trial. Management also mentioned interest from European sarcoma experts for an externally funded trial, while the company ended 2023 with $24 million in cash, sufficient into Q4 2024. The tone is confident, emphasizing superior efficacy versus approved targeted therapies and a clear regulatory pathway.

Management remains confident in market fundamentals, citing low order books and supportive demand, and highlighted a strong cash balance of $35.6 million with no bank debt.

NRE payment plan expanded to ~$95 million; cash at $85.4 million
summary: Q1 2025 revenues were a record $17.4 million, up ~3x sequentially and ~2.5x year-over-year, with record gross margin of ~40%, driven by NRE payments and LiDAR sales. The company expanded its NRE payment plan from ~$80 million to ~$95 million, ended Q1 with $85.4 million in cash, and maintained full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $50-60 million (more than twofold YoY growth). Management highlighted a new manufacturing partnership with Fabrinet, accelerated LiDAR shipments to Volkswagen for robotaxi deployments, and expanding collaboration with NVIDIA. They expect first Fabrinet product unit shipments within a month and continue to target 1-3 new programs in 2025.

negative_highlights: Israel Innovation Authority grant declined to $25,000 from $209,000 year-over-year
Gross margin may vary with mix; expected range 72%-76%
positive_highlights: Record Q1 revenue of $16.6 million, up 17.5% year-over-year
Raising full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance to 15%-18%
Highest-ever non-GAAP operating income of $3.1 million and $4.4 million positive cash flow
summary: RADCOM reported record Q1 2025 revenue of $16.6 million, up 17.5% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating income of $3.1 million (19% of revenue) and cash flow of $4.4 million, ending the quarter with $99.1 million in cash and no debt. The company raised its full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance from 12%-15% to 15%-18% year-over-year, citing strong momentum and strategic partnerships with ServiceNow and Nvidia. Management highlighted expanding agentic AI capabilities and a renewed tier-one North American contract.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.5 million from $1.8 million
Tissue Health Plus segment adjusted EBITDA loss deepened to $2.0 million
SG&A expenses increased 32% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Net revenue up 26% year-over-year to $23.4 million
Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 92%
Sanara Surgical segment adjusted EBITDA up $1.5 million to $2.7 million
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q1 2025 net revenue of $23.4 million, up 26% year-over-year, with soft tissue repair products up 28% and bone fusion up 18%. Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 92%, and Sanara Surgical segment adjusted EBITDA rose to $2.7 million from $1.2 million. The company reaffirmed its growth expectations, narrowed THP cash investment guidance, and remains on track to launch the THP pilot in Q2. Net loss widened to $3.5 million due to higher SG&A and interest expense.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell sharply to $7.5M from $17.1M YoY, partly due to a one-time 2024 Roche license
Net loss widened to $20.7M from $11.5M in Q1 2024
A $2.5M pharma biocatalysis order slipped into April, missing the top of Q1 guidance
positive_highlights: Product gross margin expanded to 55% from 49% YoY
First ligase order delivered to a large pharma customer in Q1, with additional orders expected
Three CDMOs validated ligase performance in-house, supporting scalability
summary: Codexis reported Q1 FY2025 total revenue of $7.5 million, down from $17.1 million in Q1 2024, with product gross margin up to 55% from 49%. Net loss widened to $20.7 million from $11.5 million, and cash stood at $59.8 million. The company reiterated its 2025 revenue guidance of $64–68 million, noting revenue timing was affected by a $2.5 million payment shifting to April. Management highlighted early commercial progress in its ECO platform, including first orders for its ligase products and upcoming presentations at TIDES USA.

negative_highlights: Cash only $8 million, sufficient into Q3; need $15 million more
EMA approval contingent on additional GLP studies that may impact EU timeline
Phase 2 MB-106 first patient relapsed after over 600 days of complete remission
positive_highlights: First patient treated in Phase 3 MIRACLE trial with 38 sites selected
EMA approved trial in all nine EU countries
FDA feedback reduced Part B enrollment to 222 patients
summary: Moleculin Biotech reported Q1 2025 progress with its Phase 3 MIRACLE trial for Annamycin (naxtarubicin) in relapsed/refractory AML, including first patient treated, 38 sites selected, EMA approval for nine EU countries, and WHO recognition of the generic name. The company has roughly $8 million cash, enough into Q3, and needs about $15 million to reach Q1 2026 funding. FDA feedback reduced Part B enrollment to 222 patients. Final data from the MB-107 soft tissue sarcoma trial is expected soon. The company remains confident in achieving the 45-patient interim readout by end of 2025.

negative_highlights: Israeli revenue declined 56% YoY, partly due to supply delays and the Oranim deal cancellation.
Cash balance remains low at $1.4 million, with reliance on credit facilities and future financing.
Revenue growth was modest at 4% YoY, as German gains were mostly offset by Israeli declines.
positive_highlights: Achieved net profit of $0.2 million and positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.6 million, a ~$3M improvement YoY.
German revenue grew 569% YoY, now 62% of total revenue; 12 new strains launched in Q1 alone.
Gross profit up 94% YoY, aided by a 56% reduction in operating expenses.
summary: IM Cannabis reported Q1 2025 revenues of $12.5 million, up 4% YoY, with a net profit of $0.2 million versus a $6.0 million loss a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.6 million, improving from a $2.2 million loss in Q1 2024. German revenue surged 569% YoY to offset a 56% decline in Israel, while gross margin improved 87 percentage points. Operating expenses fell 56% YoY, driving the profitability turnaround.

negative_highlights: NII per share down $0.10 QoQ to $0.45
Non-accruals increased to 3.5% of debt at cost
Tariff uncertainty tempering near-term M&A activity
positive_highlights: New investments at 565 bps spread, above recent quarters
Portfolio weighted average interest coverage improved to 2.0x
97% floating-rate assets vs. 55% floating-rate liabilities
summary: Q1 FY2025 NII was $0.45 per share, down from $0.55 in Q4, driven by lower base rates, non-recurring income runoff, reduced Logan JV dividend, and higher non-accruals. Non-accruals rose to 3.5% of debt at cost (1.8% at fair value) with four new first-lien names. Management called this quarter 'reflective of our earnings baseline,' cited tariff-driven M&A slowdown, and noted potential tailwinds from SPV facility repricing and full-quarter portfolio impact. GAAP EPS was $0.11, NAV per share $19.62.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined to $1.6M from $2.2M year-over-year.
Net loss widened to $737K in Q1 '25 vs. $573K prior year.
Year-over-year comparisons hurt by $1.2M prior-year contract and EMEA transition.
positive_highlights: Revenue up 10% sequentially to $1.6 million in Q1 '25.
Gross margin healthy at 82.6%; SG&A reduced 23% year-over-year.
Cash increased to over $3 million, and debt more than halved to ~$762K.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue fell to $1.6M from $2.2M year-over-year due to a large financial services customer's contract timing, though revenue rose 10% sequentially. The customer upgraded to a one-to-many biometric solution, contributing $690K in Q1 and expected to generate ~$3M over two years starting Q1 2026. Gross margin dipped to 82.6%, and net loss widened to $737K due to higher share count, while cash rose to $3.1M from warrant proceeds. The company is shifting to BIO-key branded products in EMEA and highlights expanding recurring revenue over $6M.

negative_highlights: Q2 sales down 20% YoY, worse than planned
Adjusted EBITDA fell from $12.3 million to $2.3 million in the quarter
U.S. customer planogram resets delayed by two months; tariff uncertainty persists
positive_highlights: Gross margins strong at 32.8% in Q2
International sales up 33% in first half, Europe up 65%
First-half adjusted EBITDA improved to $2.7 million from a loss of $4.9 million
summary: JAKKS Pacific reported Q2 2025 sales down 20% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $2.3 million versus $12.3 million last year, and adjusted EPS of $0.03 versus $0.65. The quarter was hit by tariff-driven order cancellations and delayed retail resets, but first-half sales were down only 3% overall, with international sales up 33% and Europe up 65%. Management is cautious about the second half, citing ongoing tariff uncertainty and later shelf resets, but highlighted strong gross margins of 32.8%, a new credit facility, and continued dividend.

negative_highlights: Betterware Mexico gross margin down 127 bps YoY due to pricing
Jafra US revenue down 8.9% YoY in USD
Net debt-to-EBITDA at 1.97x, above 1.8x year-ago
positive_highlights: Betterware Mexico first net associate growth since Q1 2021, up 3.3% QoQ
Jafra Mexico revenue up 10.9% YoY, EBITDA margin 21.2%
Free cash flow MXN 592 million in Q2, 87% conversion
summary: BeFra reported Q2 2025 consolidated revenue growth of 5.1% YoY and EBITDA up 3.5% YoY to MXN 679 million, with margin at 19.1%, rebounding from a weak Q1. Betterware Mexico returned to sequential growth (+4% QoQ) and achieved its first net associate growth since Q1 2021, while Jafra Mexico grew revenue 10.9% YoY with EBITDA margin at 21.2%. Guidance for 2025 is maintained at 6-9% revenue and EBITDA growth, implying acceleration in H2. Management highlighted pricing, product, and incentive initiatives as key drivers, despite a still challenging macro environment.

negative_highlights: EPS of $0.02, well below prior periods; management acknowledges disappointment
Provision remains elevated at $10M-$11M per quarter for H2 2025, and $37M-$40M for 2026
SBA gain on sale down ~$7M linked quarter; premium softness (mid-7% vs >8% historically)
positive_highlights: Net interest income up 11.5% sequentially; NIM up 14bps to 1.96% GAAP (2.04% FTE)
SBA past dues dropped 48% linked quarter; deferral dollar value down >60% from Q4 2024
July SBA sales already $52M with $3.7M gain; Q3/Q4 noninterest income forecast ~$13.3M each
summary: Q2 2025 diluted EPS was $0.02 due to elevated credit costs, despite net interest income and margin improvement. NIM rose to 2.04% FTE, with loan yields up and deposit costs down. Guidance for Q3/Q4 shows NIM expanding to 2.20%-2.35% FTE and noninterest income recovering as SBA loan sales resume (already sold $52M in July). 2026 EPS guidance is $5.20-$6.30, with elevated provision of $37M-$40M, although management noted the provision may be padded.

negative_highlights: Reported net income included a $7.5 million gain, masking noise from consumer program reversals
Core expenses rose to $22.7 million from $20.4 million in Q1, though normalized to ~$21 million
Loan growth expected to slow in back half; management cautions against extrapolating 12-15% growth
positive_highlights: Core NIM expanded to 3.15%, up from 3.13% last quarter and 2.80% a year ago
Noninterest-bearing deposits increased $22 million or 19% annualized
Technology savings expected to lower run rate by $1.5 million per quarter
summary: Primis Financial reported Q2 2025 net income of $8.4 million or $0.34 per share, including a $7.5 million pretax gain from PFH, offset by new mortgage team support and consumer program reversals. Core pretax pre-provision earnings were about $8.4 million, with core net interest margin expanding to 3.15% and noninterest-bearing deposits up 19% annualized. Management expects run-rate PPNR to grow to over $13 million heading into 2026, aided by tech savings of $1.5 million per quarter starting in Q3 and continued margin expansion to mid-3.20% by year-end.

negative_highlights: Operating profit down to $2.1 million from $4 million due to higher marketing expenses.
EPS reduced by $0.13 in Q2 from immediate member acquisition costs.
Travel industry demand is soft, with flight and hotel prices coming down.
positive_highlights: Revenue up 13% YoY to $23.9 million, growth across all segments.
Jack's Flight Club revenue increased 33% YoY; premium subscribers up 15%.
Management expects revenue growth to accelerate and profitability to substantially increase over time.
summary: Travelzoo reported Q2 2025 revenue of $23.9 million, up 13% YoY (12% in constant currency), but operating profit fell to $2.1 million from $4 million due to heavy investment in Club Member acquisition. Membership fees grew to $3 million and are expected to reach about 25% of revenue next year. Management expects revenue growth to accelerate in coming quarters as membership fees are recognized ratably, with profitability to increase over time. Despite near-term EPS pressure, they will continue aggressive member acquisition as long as payback remains favorable.

negative_highlights: Roughly $11 million of incremental tariffs on balance sheet, hitting mostly Q4
Retail gross margin down 170 bps to 45.2%
Georgia Boot finished down modestly due to tariff-related shipment delay
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS tripled to $0.55 from $0.17 a year ago
Gross margin up 230 bps to 41.0% on strong full-price note
Guidance raised: revenue growth now 4-5% and EPS up ~10%
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q2 FY2025 net sales of $105.6 million, up 7.5% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $0.55 versus $0.17 last year, more than tripling. Gross margin expanded 230 basis points to 41.0%, driven by higher wholesale margins and a favorable retail mix. The company raised its full-year 2025 guidance: revenue growth now 4-5% (up from low single digits) and EPS up ~10% to $2.79 (vs prior down slightly), despite expecting ~$11 million of tariff headwinds. Management cited strong execution across XTRATUF, Muck, and other brands, and is ahead of schedule shifting production to lower-tariff facilities like the Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico.

negative_highlights: Gas cylinders sales down 6% YoY
Automotive softness and clean energy demand subdued
FX and higher operating expenses offset gains by $2.4 million
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 25% YoY to $0.30, ahead of expectations
Elektron sales up 19% YoY; defense/first response/healthcare up 43%
Guidance raised: EPS $0.97–$1.05 and EBITDA $49–$52 million
summary: Luxfer reported Q2 2025 adjusted EPS of $0.30, up 25% YoY and 30% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $14 million (14.4% margin, up from 12.5% in Q1). Sales rose 5.8% to $97.1 million, driven by Elektron (+19% YoY) and a solid rebound in gas cylinders (up 14% sequentially). The company raised its full-year 2025 EPS guidance to $0.97–$1.05 and EBITDA to $49–$52 million, citing defense and aerospace momentum, while noting softness in autos and clean energy.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue down 19% YoY
Global retail sales down 15% YoY
Touring faced headwinds with market share decline
positive_highlights: HDFS transaction expected to add $275-$300M operating income in 2025
Cash generated to accelerate $500M buyback in H2 '25
New small-displacement bike targeted below $6,000 and expected to be profitable
summary: Harley-Davidson reported Q2 FY2025 consolidated revenue down 19% YoY, with global retail down 15%, amid elevated interest rates and demand softness. The company announced a strategic HDFS partnership with KKR and PIMCO, watching equity at ~1.75x book value and generating ~$1.25B distribution, expected to boost HDFS operating income by $275-300M in 2025. Guidance for retail in North America is expected to turn positive in the second half, supported by easier comps. Management also confirmed a new small-displacement motorcycle entry price below $6,000 launching in H1 2026.

negative_highlights: Q2 was lowest volume quarter with higher organic decline in larger print product lines
Tariffs and postal rate uncertainty remain headwinds
Rising postal rates continue to challenge clients
positive_highlights: Revenue decline of 3% within the better end of 2-6% guidance range
Expecting increasing volumes and higher revenue/EBITDA in Q3 and Q4, with Q4 highest
No significant client pullback from tariffs; cautious optimism in market
summary: Quad's Q2 FY2025 results met expectations, with revenue decline of 3% year-over-year, within the 2-6% guidance range. Management reiterated FY guidance, expecting higher revenue and EBITDA in Q3 and Q4, with Q4 as the highest. They noted cautious optimism in the market, no significant client pullback due to tariffs, and highlighted growth in data-driven marketing solutions and In-store Connect. Asset sales and acquisitions (Sacramento plant sale, Enru purchase) were completed in the quarter.

negative_highlights: U.S. revenue growth only 6% YoY, below expectations
Full-year revenue guidance lowered from $96-98M to $90-92M
Gross margin declined to 72% from 74% due to geographic mix shift
positive_highlights: International revenue $9.1M, up 32% YoY, a record
StratX referrals rebounded to record levels in June and July
Direct-to-patient campaigns engaged 70,000 patients; TAS territories saw 19% increase in workups
summary: Q2 2025 revenue was $23.9 million, up 15% YoY and 13% on a constant currency basis, with international revenue a record $9.1 million, up 32% YoY. U.S. revenue grew only 6% to $14.7 million, missing expectations due to slower procedure volume growth, declined StratX scans, and capacity constraints at interventional pulmonology centers. Management lowered full-year 2025 revenue guidance from $96-98 million to $90-92 million, attributing the shortfall to timing rather than strategic changes and citing record StratX referrals in June/July as early signs of improvement.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $13M in Q2 2025, compared to net income of $36M a year ago
Sales down 8% YoY due to 22% lower Brent prices
Guidance at lower end; first-half average of 47,000 BOE/d near the bottom of 47,000-53,000 range
positive_highlights: Record production of 47,200 BOE/d, up 44% YoY
Lowest operating cost per BOE since early 2022
Signed $200M prepayment facility mandate to address 2026 debt maturity
summary: Gran Tierra reported record production of 47,200 BOE/d (up 44% YoY), but net loss widened to $13M due to lower Brent prices. Operating costs per BOE hit the lowest since early 2022, and funds flow from operations rose 17% YoY. The company signed a mandate for a $200M prepayment facility and expects closing in Q3 2025, while maintaining 2025 production guidance of 47,000-53,000 BOE/d. Management highlighted strong results from Cohembi, Costayaco, and Simonette, and expressed confidence in ramping production in H2.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guided to at or near low end of previous range
Producer mechanical issue remediation slower than expected, wells to remain down until end of Q3
Blue water marine market softened with incremental supply, limiting day rate increases
positive_highlights: Shenandoah delivered first oil, initial wells expected to meet/exceed predrill expectations
Salamanca on track for first oil by end of Q3 2025
Free cash flow generation expected to begin in Q3 2025, with 2026 outlook unchanged
summary: Genesis Energy reported Q2 2025 results in line with expectations but guided to the low end of prior adjusted EBITDA guidance due to delayed producer well remediation and slightly delayed first oil from Shenandoah and Salamanca. Shenandoah achieved first oil last week with initial wells expected to exceed predrill expectations and ramp to 100,000 barrels per day by end of September; Salamanca remains on track for first oil by end of Q3. Management reaffirmed 2026 outlook and expects free cash flow generation to begin in Q3, with focus on deleveraging and potential capital returns to unitholders.

negative_highlights: Fourth quarter expected to see more tariff cost flow-through
Watercraft marketplace remains weak and industry struggles
Diving marketplace challenged with uncertainties
positive_highlights: Sales up 5% to $180.7 million versus the prior year
Operating profit swung to $7.3 million from an operating loss
Gross margin up 1.8 points to 37.6%
summary: Johnson Outdoors reported Q3 FY2025 net sales of $180.7 million, up 5% year-over-year, with operating profit of $7.3 million versus an operating loss a year ago. Gross margin expanded 1.8 points to 37.6%, driven by higher volumes, pricing, and cost savings, partly offset by tariffs. Management noted strong demand for new fishing innovations and Jetboil products, but cautioned on fourth-quarter tariff costs and a still-weak watercraft market. The company remains debt-free and is focused on cost savings and tariff mitigation.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 18% on constant currency basis
North America gross margin pressured by input costs and inefficiencies; 540 bps decline
Europe/APAC combined revenue down 2.7% with flat volumes, EU tariffs and destocking
positive_highlights: Eighth consecutive quarter of volume growth, with 5.2% volume growth overall
Automation revenue increased 34% with robust backlog; full year $40-$45 million expected
Potential multiyear North America deal worth over $100 million could consume Shelton capacity
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue grew 3.8% on a constant currency basis, with North America up 12.2% and volumes up 14.8%, but adjusted EBITDA declined 18% due to input cost, mix, and inefficiencies. The company is executing $8 million in cost-out actions and expects margin and EBITDA improvement in H2, with automation revenue guided to $40-$45 million. A potential multiyear North America automation deal worth over $100 million was highlighted, but no formal guidance was raised.

negative_highlights: Arcadia sales down 11% YoY on weak high-end residential demand
NobelClad backlog fell to $37 million from $41 million due to tariff-driven lost business
Third-quarter guidance implies sales down $5-13 million sequentially and EBITDA down $1.5-5.5 million
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $13.5 million exceeded the $10-13 million guidance range
Total debt reduced 17% sequentially to $59 million
DynaEnergetics adjusted EBITDA margin rose 210 bps sequentially and 190 bps YoY to 13.4%
summary: DMC Global reported Q2 FY2025 consolidated sales of $155.5 million and adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC of $13.5 million, exceeding the guidance range of $10 million to $13 million. Arcadia sales declined 11% YoY, DynaEnergetics declined 12%, while NobelClad grew 6% but saw backlog fall to $37 million from $41 million. The company cut total debt by 17% to $59 million. Third-quarter guidance is soft at $142-150 million sales and $8-12 million EBITDA due to tariff uncertainty, high interest rates, and weak energy activity.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin declined to 49% from 54% due to amortization and warranty costs
Adjusted gross margin down 220 basis points to 56% driven by higher warranty costs
Operating expenses increased to $21.5 million from $14.7 million due to noncash charges
positive_highlights: Revenue up 14% YoY to $13 million, above internal expectations
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved 45% YoY and 15% QoQ
Record XplorIR units shipped in Q2, with 164 devices placed
summary: 908 Devices reported Q2 2025 revenue of $13 million, up 14% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA loss improving 45% year-over-year and 15% sequentially. The company highlighted record XplorIR placements and strong legislative tailwinds, while maintaining its goal of adjusted EBITDA positive by Q4 2025. They launched VipIR, acquired KAF Manufacturing, and completed facility consolidations to reduce costs.

negative_highlights: CHMP referral raises questions on tecovirimat efficacy for mpox
International orders expected to remain lumpy
US government RFP timing uncertain, with negotiation expected to take months
positive_highlights: Product revenues of $79M in Q2, fulfilling $70M of outstanding orders
Received $27M in incremental development funding from US government
Pretax operating income of $46M and net income of $35M, with no debt
summary: Q2 2025 product revenue was $79 million (oral TPOXX $53M, IV TPOXX $26M), fulfilling $70M of prior-year orders, with $26M in remaining IV TPOXX orders targeted for 2026 delivery. Pretax operating income was $46 million for the quarter, net income $35 million, and fully diluted EPS $0.49. The U.S. government committed $27 million in incremental development funding under the BARDA 19C contract ($14M manufacturing, $13M pediatric). The CHMP initiated a referral on tecovirimat efficacy for mpox, while management remains confident in the smallpox indication.

negative_highlights: Lift Truck revenues declined 19% year-over-year, with volumes down across all product lines
Q2 bookings fell to $330 million from $590 million in Q1, driven by tariff-related demand deferrals
Q2 adjusted operating profit down to $5 million, with tariff-driven costs of $10 million
positive_highlights: Operating cash flow improved to ~$30 million in Q2, up from prior year and prior quarter
Unused borrowing capacity increased 3% to nearly $260 million
Bolzoni revenue grew sequentially with improved margins from mix shift
summary: In Q2 FY2025, Hyster-Yale reported Lift Truck revenues down 19% year-over-year, with adjusted operating profit falling sharply to $5 million, impacted by $10 million in tariff-driven costs. Bookings declined to $330 million from $590 million in Q1, and backlog fell from $1.9 billion to $1.7 billion. The company maintained its full-year guidance but emphasized heightened economic uncertainty, tariff volatility, and a cyclical demand trough, while planning to increase production in H2 to meet an expected demand uptick.

negative_highlights: Gross originations declined to $48 million from $166 million quarter-over-quarter
Net investment income fell to $0.46 per share from $0.53 due to fee changes
Net asset value declined from $17.96 to $17.92 per share on valuation losses
positive_highlights: Net investment income of $0.46 per share exceeded the quarterly distribution of $0.45
Nonaccruals improved to 0.2% of fair value, down from 0.4%
Pipeline increasing with deal reviews up over 60% from April to June
summary: NCDL reported Q2 2025 net investment income of $0.46 per share, covering its $0.45 dividend, but down from $0.53 in Q1 due to the expiration of an incentive fee waiver and intentional leverage reduction. Gross originations fell to $48 million from $166 million, reflecting a deliberate slowdown, with portfolio fair value down slightly to $2 billion. Credit quality improved with nonaccruals dropping to 0.2% of fair value, and NAV dipped to $17.92 per share. Management sees positive momentum in the second half with a stronger pipeline and completed rotation to core middle market assets.

negative_highlights: Book value per share decreased to negative $43.14 from negative $40.99.
Corporate unencumbered cash fell to $355 million from $380 million at year-end.
PREPA resolution timing remains uncertain; Oversight Board changes add unpredictability.
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss narrowed to $56 million from $254 million year-over-year.
Transferred $374 million of PREPA claims to custodian to improve marketability.
National statutory capital rose to $914 million from $912 million at year-end.
summary: MBIA reported a narrower GAAP net loss of $56 million in Q2 2025 versus $254 million a year ago, primarily due to lower losses on PREPA exposure. Adjusted net loss was $8 million, improved from $138 million last year. Book value per share declined to negative $43.14 from negative $40.99. Management emphasized persistent PREPA uncertainty and noted a newly transferred $374 million of PREPA claims to a custodian to enhance marketability, while still considering the sale process. Guidance is not applicable, but tone is cautious and forward-looking about PREPA resolution.

negative_highlights: No revenue or product sales; company is pre-commercialization
Cash balance decreased to $379.7 million from prior periods (interest income lower)
Phase III data not available until 2026
positive_highlights: Phase II results demonstrated 98% SVR12 in primary efficacy analysis with 8-week treatment
Enrollment in Phase III trials is on track; top-line data expected mid-2026 and end of 2026
Market research: 76% of high U.S. DAA prescribers extremely likely to prescribe regimen
summary: Atea Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 2025 progress with its HCV regimen bemnifosbuvir/ruzavir, highlighting 98% SVR12 in the primary efficacy analysis at EASL. Phase III enrollment is on track, with top-line results expected mid-2026 (C-BEYOND) and end of 2026 (C-FORWARD). Cash balance is $379.7 million, with runway through 2027, and the company repurchased 4.6 million shares under a $25 million buyback. Market research shows 76% of high U.S. DAA prescribers extremely likely to prescribe the regimen.

negative_highlights: Ting adjusted EBITDA loss of $3.7M in Q2, though improved YoY before noncash lease adjustment.
Corporate net debt high at $190.3M; leverage 3.14x, though declining.
Macro signals mixed; management remains cautious and conservative.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue up 10% YoY to $98.5M, fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth.
Wavelo delivered best quarter ever: revenue +21% YoY, adjusted EBITDA +37% YoY.
New Radix registry contract to migrate >10M domains, boosting registry to ~17M domains.
summary: Tucows Q2 FY2025 revenue grew 10% YoY to $98.5M, with gross profit up 6% to $22.1M (absorbing a $2.7M noncash lease adjustment at Ting) and adjusted EBITDA up 37% to $12.6M. Year-to-date adjusted EBITDA of $26.2M is slightly ahead of the run-rate for full-year guidance of $47M. Domains and Wavelo outperformed, with Wavelo posting its best quarter (revenue +21% YoY, EBITDA +37%). Ting revenue grew 13% with subscribers up 8%, but remains loss-making; the company signed a landmark senior-living bulk contract and sold nonstrategic assets for over $15M. Guidance maintained.

negative_highlights: Q3 volume guidance below Q2 actuals
Gain on sale margin down to 330bps from 355bps
CEO acknowledges market share has shrunk
positive_highlights: Adjusted net loss narrowed from $25M to $16M
Origination volume up 30% sequentially
Direct origination expenses down 7% despite 30% volume increase
summary: Q2 2025 adjusted net loss narrowed to $16M from $25M in Q1 on higher lock volume and lower costs. Pull-through weighted rate lock volume was $6.3B, up 17% sequentially and within guidance; origination volume was $6.7B, up 30% and within guidance. Gain on sale margin was 330bps, down from 355bps and within guidance. Q3 guidance calls for lower volumes and margins, reflecting market volatility and high rates. CEO returned permanently and focuses on regaining market share and profitability.

negative_highlights: Q3 guidance includes a 4-point political headwind
Three major advertisers have not resumed spending; Q3 guide excludes them
Contribution ex-TAC growth (16%) lagged revenue growth (18%), partly due to deliberate pass-through of AI savings
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 18% year-over-year
Adjusted EBITDA up 18% to $11.3 million, surpassing guidance midpoint
AI Bidding contribution ex-TAC doubled year-over-year
summary: Viant reported Q2 2025 revenue up 18% YoY and contribution ex-TAC up 16% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 18% to $11.3 million, surpassing the midpoint of guidance. CTV drove growth, with Household ID spend up 15% YoY, and AI Bidding now automates 85% of ad spend. Q3 guidance implies a slowdown due to a 4-point political headwind and excludes any resumption of delayed advertiser spending, while a $250 million gross spend pipeline is expected to contribute to 2026 budgets.

negative_highlights: Production slower than Q1 due to deliberate activity reduction and completion timing
Second quarter CapEx down 30% sequentially due to dropping a rig in May
Uncertainty around adding second rig in September; retains flexibility to delay
positive_highlights: Generated over $155 million of EBITDAX in Q2 with margins of $33.58 per BOE
Refinanced term loan and RBL, extending maturities to September 2028 and boosting liquidity
Simul-frac on first pad saved ~$400,000 per well, ~10% completion cost reduction
summary: HighPeak Energy reported a solid Q2 2025 with EBITDAX over $155 million and strong margins of $33.58 per BOE, despite lower commodity prices. Production was slightly below Q1 due to planned activity reductions and completion timing, but management reaffirmed full-year 2025 production guidance. The company reduced CapEx by 30% sequentially, dropped to one rig in mid-May, and plans to add a second rig in September, though it retains flexibility to delay. They completed a debt refinancing extending maturities to 2028 and added hedges covering over 50% of H2 volumes at a weighted average floor above $62.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 53% from 67% due to revenue mix
Marketplace revenue soft at $0.3 million due to halted marketing spend
Credit business revenue declined year-over-year
positive_highlights: Revenue up 18% YoY, with fintech up 28% excluding one-time vendor true-up
First-half net loss improved 46% to $12.8 million
Realized $9M of $11M annualized cost savings in H1
summary: Q2 FY2025 net revenue was $7.1 million, up 18% YoY, with Fintech revenue at $3.4 million (up 15.6%, but would have been $3.8 million or 28% without a $0.4 million vendor true-up), Brands/EveryLife at $3.3 million (up 45.5%), and Marketplace soft at $0.3 million. Gross margin declined to 53% from 67% due to mix. GAAP operating loss improved to $8.1 million from $14 million, and net loss per share improved to -$0.18 from -$0.36. Management announced plans to monetize EveryLife and Marketplace to focus entirely on fintech, expecting completion by Q4 2025. First-half OpEx declined 13% and net loss improved 46%, with $9 million of the expected $11 million annualized savings realized in H1.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $2.1 million from $3.6 million
Gearing segment reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.1 million
Guidance suspended due to pending asset sale

Gearing orders up 45% and $6 million follow-on order received in July
summary: Q2 2025 revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $39.2 million, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $2.1 million from $3.6 million, with margin down to 5.3% due to capacity inefficiencies. Orders grew 14% to $21 million, with Industrial Solutions setting a record for orders and backlog. The company suspended full-year guidance due to the pending sale of Manitowoc, expecting $13 million cash and $8 million annual cost savings. Gearing continued to rebound with a new $6 million order in July.

negative_highlights: NAUTILUS missed primary effectiveness endpoint in earlier time-to-event analysis

Executive transition incurred onetime nonrecurring items
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $23.5M, up 22% YoY
Raised full-year revenue and gross margin guidance
NAUTILUS data showing >80% median GTC seizure reduction at 18-24 months and 45.2% seizure-free at 12 months
summary: NeuroPace reported record Q2 2025 revenue of $23.5 million, up 22% year-over-year, with total gross margin above 77% and RNS gross margin above 80%. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to $94-$98 million and gross margin to 75%-76%, citing strong RNS System sales and Project CARE expansion. Management highlighted compelling NAUTILUS data for IGE, with median GTC seizure reduction signaling better than 80% at 18 and 24 months and 45.2% seizure-free at 12 months, and reaffirmed PMA supplement submission in H2 2025. They also completed a refinancing and noted positive CMS IPPS outcome preserving current DRG reimbursement.

negative_highlights: Revenue guidance for 2025 maintained at $64-68 million, implying significant back-half weighted performance
Management notes continued lumpiness in Pharma Biocatalysis revenue due to unpredictable order timing
Gross margin improvement to 72% is not expected to be sustained at that magnitude for the full year
positive_highlights: Revenue in Q2 2025 was $15.3 million, nearly double the $8 million reported in Q2 2024
Operating loss halved year-over-year, with net loss improving to $13.3 million from $23.8 million
Customer engagements for ECO Synthesis exceed 30, with growing interest approaching 40
summary: Codexis reported Q2 2025 revenue of $15.3 million, up from $8 million in Q2 2024, with product gross margin expanding to 72% from 45%. Net loss narrowed to $13.3 million from $23.8 million year-over-year. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $64-68 million, with growth expected in the second half from ligase and ECO Synthesis. They reported over 30 (approaching 40) customer engagements for ECO Synthesis and are exploring options to expand capacity, including a potential Codexis-owned GMP facility to capture more value from early-phase projects.

Operating loss of $5 million in Q2 2025
SG&A reduction partially offset by higher R&D costs

Closed $600,000 follow-on orders from defense ministry, total project over EUR 3 million
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue increased 49% year-over-year to $1.7 million, with hardware revenue up $458,000, but gross margin declined to 73% from 77% due to product mix. SG&A was reduced 13.5% year-over-year, partially offset by higher R&D, and the company reduced its note payable from $1.5 million to $447,000. Management highlighted new defense contracts, including a first phase deployment for an international defense agency, a 3-year PortalGuard deployment with a Middle East police force, and $600,000 of follow-on orders. Despite a $5 million operating loss in Q2, management expects expense run rate to normalize and sees strong growth opportunities in defense and EMEA in the back half of 2025.

negative_highlights: Gross margin only 16% in Q2, with fluctuation expected
Cash burn still $7.3 million in quarter; annualized burn remains

summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue was $9.7 million, up 46% year-over-year, with first-half revenue of $27.1 million exceeding all of FY2024. Cash burn fell to $7.3 million from $20.7 million in Q1, and the company raised its NRE booking guidance to $30-60 million from $20-50 million. Management launched the InnovizSMART non-automotive product and signed a development agreement with a top-5 OEM for a 2027 L3 program, while maintaining full-year revenue guidance of $50-60 million. The company is ramping production at Fabrinet and expects 10x unit shipments in Q3 versus Q2.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net loss only improved 43% due to continued THP investment

summary: Sanara MedTech's Surgical segment grew net revenue 28% YoY to $25.8 million, with soft tissue up 28% and bone fusion up 25%. The segment achieved about $500,000 net income, a $2.7 million improvement, and adjusted EBITDA rose 239% to $4.7 million. Management initiated a formal strategic alternatives process for THP and guided second-half THP cash investment down to $5.5-$6.5 million. The company remains on track for OsStic launch in Q1 2027 after BMI completed two milestones.

FX headwinds from shekel strength noted, not hedged

Cash at record $101.6 million, debt-free
summary: RADCOM reported record Q2 2025 revenue of $17.7 million, up 19.3% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating income of $3.4 million (19.5% of revenue) and non-GAAP net income of $4.2 million ($0.25 per diluted share). Cash reached a record $101.6 million, with positive operating cash flow of $2.6 million. The company maintained full-year revenue guidance of 15-18% growth and noted progress on NVIDIA and ServiceNow partnerships, with some customers moving to lab deployments.

negative_highlights: Guest value perception declined unexpectedly after March menu launch
Company comp traffic down 2.5% in Q2; July started at -0.9%
Full-year guidance lowered; no longer free cash flow positive in 2025

Owned digital traffic up 2% YoY and rewards check-ins up 4% in Q2
Portfolio closures are removing negative-cash-flow restaurants and boosting nearby sales
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q2 FY2025 total revenue of $126.4 million, down 0.7% YoY, with system-wide comp sales up 1.5% but traffic down 2.5%. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $6 million from $9.2 million, and restaurant contribution margin contracted to 12.8% from 15.5%, pressured by $1.7 million in menu-rollout costs. Management cut full-year guidance to revenue of $487-$495 million and comp sales growth of 2.5%-4%, and no longer expects positive free cash flow in 2025. Recent weekly sales trends improved to +5% following the Duos value launch, but overall results missed internal expectations.

summary: CCAP reported Q2 2025 NII of $0.46 per share, or $0.48 excluding $0.02 of one-time accelerated amortization, up from $0.45 in Q1. NAV per share declined 0.4% to $19.55, largely due to a special dividend, with stable portfolio yield at 10.4% and debt-to-equity at 1.23x. Deal activity was constrained, gross deployment was $58 million with net realizations of $35 million, and the company announced a $20 million stock repurchase program. Management noted watch list at 14% of portfolio at fair value, nonaccruals at 2.4%, and no Q3 supplemental dividend.

negative_highlights: Revenue flat year-over-year and below expectations

positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 73% from 64% year-over-year

CAPTAIN trial fully enrolled with 212 patients; TULSA-AI BPH software on track for Q4 launch
summary: Profound Medical reported Q2 2025 revenue of $2.2 million, flat year-over-year, with a net loss widening to $15.7 million ($0.52/share) from $6.9 million ($0.28/share) in Q2 2024. Total orders were over $3 million, and gross margin improved to 73% from 64%. Management acknowledged revenue was below expectations due to delays in capital sales but reiterated full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance of 70-75% over 2024. Key milestones include full enrollment of the CAPTAIN trial (212 patients) and pilot launch of TULSA-AI BPH software with 60-90 minute procedure times.

Pediatrics grew 23%, while heart failure and critical care declined 53% and 35%. Gross margin fell to 55.5% from 67.2%, and operating loss widened to $2.9 million. The company terminated REVERSE-HF to reallocate funds and plans a manufacturing transition, while noting progress in outpatient heart failure with improved reimbursement.

Treasury unrealized gains of $7.8 million
summary: Q2 2025 asset management fees were $30 million, up from $28.3 million in Q2 2024, with adjusted EBITDA of $26.3 million and profit after tax of $32.4 million. Fee-paying AUM rose 26% quarter-over-quarter to $6.6 billion, driven by strong price recovery and $170 million inflows into CoinShares Physical, which offset XBT outflows. The company highlighted positive momentum into H2, including new all-time highs in July and progress on U.S. expansion and product pipeline.

summary: Aviat Networks reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $115.3 million, down 1.1% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.83 (up 15.3%) and record adjusted EBITDA of $15.1 million, up 26.7%. Backlog rose 11% to $323 million. Fiscal 2026 guidance implies roughly 4% revenue growth at the midpoint, with management citing conservatism due to lumpy project demand; they also disclosed material weaknesses in internal controls.

Mexican consumer environment described as sluggish and volatile
Year-to-date EBITDA still below last year's level due to a difficult Q1

summary: In Q3 FY2025, revenue grew 1.4% year-over-year, EBITDA increased 22% with margin expanding 362 basis points to 21.4%, and adjusted net income rose 71%. Management highlighted solid profitability, strong free cash flow conversion at 77% of EBITDA, and declining leverage (1.97x to 1.8x). Betterware Mexico sales decreased 5.3% due to softer demand, while Jafra Mexico grew 8% with EBITDA up 31%. Guidance for full-year EBITDA growth of 1% to 5% was reiterated, with expectations for inventory reductions and continued international expansion.

Net interest income up 8% linked quarter, up 40% year-over-year

summary: Third quarter 2025 included a $41.6 million net loss, with adjusted net loss of $12.5 million. Revenue grew to $43.5 million adjusted total, and net interest income rose 8% linked quarter and 40% year-over-year. The bank sold $837 million in STL loans, recognized $34.8 million provision with $21 million charge-offs, and guided to full-year 2026 NII around $149-150 million, citing strong pipelines and deposit cost reductions.

negative_highlights: Reported ROA of 70bps still below 1% target

Adjusted ROA ~90bps, on track to 1% target
summary: Primis Financial reported Q3 2025 net earnings of $6.8 million or $0.28 per share, up from core income of $2 million a year ago. Reported ROA improved to 70 bps, but adjusted ROA was approximately 90 bps, with management targeting 1% ROA in the near term. Net interest margin expanded to 3.18% from 2.86% last quarter, and core expenses were reduced sequentially. Management raised expectations for continued margin and earnings improvement, citing strong mortgage and Panacea growth and sticky digital deposits.

summary: Rocky Brands reported Q3 FY2025 net sales up 7% to $122.5 million, with adjusted EPS of $1.03, up 34% YoY. Gross margins expanded 210 bps to 40.2% despite a 160 bps tariff headwind. Management reiterated full-year guidance of 4-5% revenue growth, gross margins of 38-39%, and EPS up ~10%. They expect Q4 2025 to be the worst tariff impact quarter, with headwinds abating by mid-2026.

The company invested heavily in acquiring Club Members, with acquisition costs rising to $40 per member, reducing EPS by $0.15. Management expects revenue growth to accelerate and membership fees to account for about 25% of revenue next year, but cautions on short-term profit fluctuations.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 7% YoY (excluding divestiture), driven by lower paper, print, logistics, and agency sales.
Year-to-date adjusted EBITDA down to $141 million from $161 million in 2024.
Loss of a large grocery client annualized at beginning of March 2025.

USPS announcement of no January postage increase for market dominant mail.

summary: Quad's Q3 2025 net sales declined 7% YoY (excluding the Europe divestiture) to $588 million, with adjusted EBITDA down to $53 million from $59 million, though adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 8.9%. Management narrowed full-year guidance for sales, EBITDA, and cash flow, citing persistent pressures from lower print volumes, paper sales, and logistics. They noted limited tariff impact, a beneficial USPS decision not to raise postage in January, and growing momentum in In-Store Connect and direct mail, but remained cautious about 2026 planning and postage uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth modest at 1.6% YoY, with volume/mix down $0.8M
Softness persists in clean energy, automotive, and zirconium end markets
Gas Cylinders margin held near 9% with ongoing market softness
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 11% YoY to $0.30, above prior guidance trajectory
Elektron EBITDA margin expanded 160 bps to 19.8% on favorable mix
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $1.04-$1.08
summary: Luxfer reported Q3 2025 adjusted EPS of $0.30, up 11% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $13.6 million with a 14.6% margin, which expanded sequentially. Elektron was the key driver with sales up 2.5% to $50 million and EBITDA margin up 160 bps to 19.8%. The company raised its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.04-$1.08 from $0.97-$1.05, while maintaining FCF guidance of $20-$25 million. Management highlighted strength in defense and aerospace, progress on cost-saving initiatives, and continued softness in clean energy and automotive.

summary: GBank reported Q3 2025 EPS of $0.30, down $0.02 sequentially, with $2 million in unusual expenses. Net revenue grew 13.5% to $20.2 million, and loan production hit a record $242 million, but NPAs rose to 0.8% of assets. Management noted fraud-related costs and discontinued direct mail campaigns, while planning improvements in SBA incentives and digital payments. Guidance implies expense normalization and continued growth, but no explicit forward guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Marine transportation faced temporary headwinds in July and early August
One high-margin offshore field still down causing 10-15 kbd impact
Blue water fleet day rates pressured by vessel relocations
positive_highlights: Offshore segment sequential improvement of 16%
Shenandoah reached 100 kbd within 75 days of startup
Incremental offshore segment margin of about $160 million expected from Shenandoah and Salamanca
summary: In Q3 2025, Genesis Energy reported results broadly in line with expectations despite temporary marine headwinds. Offshore pipeline volumes improved sequentially by 16%, driven by first oil from Shenandoah and Salamanca, with Shenandoah reaching 100 kbd by early October. Marine segment faced temporary market softness but recovered by September/October, while onshore performed as expected. Management expects continued growth and free cash flow, with debt reduction and capital returns as priorities.

Tariff uncertainty caused retailers to delay orders by ~2 months, pushing out key note seasons

International non-U.S. year-to-date sales up 4% excluding Canada, with continued bullish outlook
Sonic-DC mashup 'flying off the shelf' and Sonic note-through strong all year
summary: Q3 2025 net sales fell sharply, with Toys/Consumer Products down 41% to $156.1 million and Costumes down 4% to $55.1 million, as tariffs and retailer delays (pushed back sets by ~2 months) slashed FOB orders. Gross margin held at 32% (down from 33.8%), SG&A fell 6%, and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $36.5 million from $74.4 million a year ago. Management remains cautious, prioritizing margins, inventory control, and cash, while pointing to international growth (YTD flat, +4% ex-Canada) and a stronger 2026-27 pipeline.

Year-end cash balance guidance lowered to $65-$70M

positive_highlights: Automation revenue up 56% constant currency, on track for $40-45M full-year
North America revenue up 10.9% with automation up 140%
Walmart and Medline partnerships expected to drive significant future growth
summary: Ranpak reported Q3 2025 net revenue growth of 4.4% constant currency, with North America up 10.9% and automation up 56% constant currency, offset by volume declines in Europe and APAC. The company announced a strategic Walmart partnership with up to $300 million in potential spend over 10 years and a Medline enterprise agreement for up to 14 distribution centers. Full-year automation guidance maintained at $40-$45 million. Adjusted EBITDA grew 3.5% constant currency, gross margin improved to 34.5%, and net leverage was 4.4x LTM. Year-end cash forecast lowered to $65-$70 million, and long-term targets include $800 million revenue in 5 years with automation at 15% and >25% EBITDA margin.

positive_highlights: Production up 30% YoY to 42,685 BOE/d

Cohembi waterflood response: north area production up 135% to 6,700 bopd
summary: Gran Tierra's Q3 2025 production averaged 42,685 BOE/d, up 30% YoY, but was temporarily impacted by external events including an Ecuador landslide and Moqueta trunk line repairs, leading to a forecast at the lower end of production guidance. Current production is recovering at 45,200 BOE/d, with an expected exit rate of 47,000-50,000 BOE/d. Operating cash flow was $48 million, up 39% from Q2, and the company secured $150 million prepayment facility and extended Canadian credit facility. Management expects a strong finish and plans a 2026 budget focused on free cash flow and deleveraging.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance unchanged despite strong Q1, citing early in the year and government shutdown
U.S. government shutdown could push out some Q2 revenue, with worst-case impact of 4-5%
Management remains cautious on December quarter, not wanting to 'get over our skis'
positive_highlights: Revenue up 21.4% YoY with non-GAAP EPS of $0.43, a $1.30 improvement over last year
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 33.8% from 23.2% year-over-year
Launched Aprisa LTE 5G router, addressing a $2.8 billion market with strong customer interest
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $107.3 million, up 21.4% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.43 and adjusted EBITDA of $9.1 million. North America revenue grew 24.7% and international grew 18.3%, with gross margin expanding to 33.8% non-GAAP from 23.2% a year ago. Management maintained full-year guidance of $440-$460 million revenue and $45-$55 million adjusted EBITDA, while expressing confidence in public safety demand and the new Aprisa LTE 5G router opportunity. They noted a minor impact from the U.S. government shutdown, with some revenue pushouts expected in Q2 but recovering in Q3.

negative_highlights: High leverage and expected material outspend over next 2-3 years
2026 production flat due to growth project timing and May 2026 turnaround
Equity dilution via $300 million rights offering
positive_highlights: Recapitalization plan to fully repay senior notes and be debt-free
Expect to hit top end of 2025 production guidance
Boiler restored ahead of schedule and sulfur removal facilities expected in November 2025
summary: Greenfire announced a transformational recapitalization plan to fully repay senior secured notes via a $300 million equity rights offering backstopped by Waterous Energy Fund and secure an upsized $275 million credit facility, leaving the company debt-free after closing. Production is expected to hit the top end of 2025 guidance of 15,000-16,000 bbl/d, with capital guidance reaffirmed at $130 million. The company approved a $180 million 2026 capital budget with flat production guidance of 15,500-16,500 bpd, due to growth projects not reaching first oil until late Q4 2026 and a planned May 2026 turnaround. The boiler outage was resolved ahead of schedule, but the second boiler is being refurbished, and sulfur removal facilities are expected operational in November 2025.

negative_highlights: Pediatric indication submission delayed beyond 2025.
DIXI sales decline expected in Q4 due to wind-down.
Operating expenses increased 21% YoY, partly due to higher note costs.
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 30% YoY to $27.4 million, a record.

The company achieved its first positive adjusted EBITDA and raised full-year revenue guidance to $97-$98 million and gross margin guidance to 76%-77%. FDA submission for NAUTILUS remains on track for year-end, but pediatric indication timelines extend beyond 2025. DIXI wind-down is progressing with lower Q4 contribution expected.

negative_highlights: NII per share declined to $0.43 from $0.46 in Q2 due to lower interest income and two new nonaccruals

positive_highlights: High-quality portfolio with nonaccruals just 0.4% of fair value and watchlist at ~7% of fair value
Churchill platform reviewed 22% more deals in Q3 vs Q2 and saw record July/August/September activity
No exposure to Tricolor or First Brands; portfolio fundamentals show solid single-digit growth
summary: NCDL reported Q3 2025 NII of $0.43 per share, down from $0.46 in Q2, and total investment income declined slightly to $51.1 million from $53.1 million. NAV per share slipped to $17.85 from $17.92, and gross originations fell to $29 million from $48 million, intentionally due to operating at the high end of leverage range. Portfolio credit quality appears stable with nonaccruals at 0.4% of fair value and top 10 positions at 13.6% of fair value, but management is optimistic about 2026 deal flow and highlights no exposure to Tricolor or First Brands.

negative_highlights: Q4 guidance implies sequential decline in revenue and EBITDA
DynaEnergetics sequential EBITDA down 46% due to tariffs and lower pricing
NobelClad sales down 16% YoY due to tariff-related slowdown
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 51% YoY to $8.6 million
Arcadia sales up 7% YoY and EBITDA more than doubled
Net debt down 47% since year-start
summary: DMC's Q3 FY2025 revenue of $151.5 million declined 1% YoY, while adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC rose 51% to $8.6 million. Arcadia grew 7% YoY and EBITDA more than doubled, but DynaEnergetics and NobelClad faced headwinds from tariffs and weak demand, with NobelClad sales down 16% YoY. The company lowered Q4 guidance to $140-150 million sales and $5-8 million EBITDA, citing continued market challenges. Net debt was reduced to $30.1 million, down 47% since the start of the year, and NobelClad won a record $20 million order (plus $5 million follow-on) that will ship in 2026.

negative_highlights: MBIA Insurance Corp. statutory net loss of $25M due to lower Zohar CDO recoveries
PREPA resolution timing uncertain with litigation over board dismissals and bondholder opposition at ~90%
Consolidated book value per share remains negative at -$43.17
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss narrowed from $56M to $8M YoY, driven by PREPA loss reserve benefit of $54M
Adjusted net income of $51M ($1.03/share) versus breakeven in prior year
National statutory capital increased $82M YTD to $994M
summary: MBIA reported a Q3 2025 GAAP net loss of $8 million, narrower than the $56 million loss a year earlier, largely due to a $54 million net benefit from PREPA loss reserves after watching $374 million of bankruptcy claims. Adjusted net income was $51 million versus breakeven a year ago. National's statutory capital rose to $994 million, while MBIA Insurance Corp. posted a statutory net loss on lower Zohar recoveries. PREPA resolution remains uncertain due to board litigation and bondholder opposition, but management believes reduced exposure improves prospects for a future sale or special dividend.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 0.5% YoY
Net loss increased to $9.2 million from $6.8 million
Food costs up 20 bps due to higher food costs
positive_highlights: October comp sales +8% with traffic +1.5%
Adjusted EBITDA up 33% to $6.5 million
Restaurant contribution margin +40 bps to 13.2%
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q3 FY2025 total revenue of $122.1 million, down 0.5% YoY, with system-wide comp sales up 4.0%. Company comp traffic declined 0.6%, but improved sequentially within the quarter and accelerated to +8% in October with traffic up over 1.5%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 33% to $6.5 million, and restaurant contribution margin expanded 40 bps. The company raised its full-year revenue and comp guidance, and is executing restaurant closures expected to positively impact 2026 margins by over $2 million.

negative_highlights: Operating profit declined by $27 million year-over-year due to lower volumes and tariffs.
Backlog fell to $1.35 billion from $1.65 billion in Q2.
Management expects further backlog degradation and softness in near-term demand.
positive_highlights: Bookings rose to $380 million in Q3, up from $330 million in Q2.
EMEA revenues increased year-over-year on higher truck sales and currency.
Operating cash flow improved by nearly 25% sequentially on better inventory.
summary: In Q3 FY2025, Hyster-Yale's lift truck revenues fell 4% year-over-year to $929 million, with operating profit down $27 million due to lower volumes and $40 million in gross tariff costs, only partially offset by pricing. Bookings rose to $380 million from $330 million in Q2, but backlog dropped sharply to $1.35 billion from $1.65 billion due to shipments outpacing bookings. Management guided for further softness in demand and additional backlog deterioration, with near-term profitability expected to decline before improving in early 2026 as tariff-affected backlog clears.

negative_highlights: Rig count reduced to 1, Wells drilled down roughly one-third from Q1/Q2
Second rig pickup delayed 1.5 months due to weak commodity prices
CEO acknowledged 'debt is high' and market confidence eroded
positive_highlights: Production levels consistent with Q2 despite reduced activity
CapEx down 30% from Q2, spot on with internal estimates
Simul-frac completion delivered over $400,000 savings per well
summary: HighPeak reported Q3 2025 results that tracked internal expectations, with production consistent with Q2 despite reduced activity, CapEx down 30% from Q2, and LOE per BOE held flat. The company ran only 1 rig during the quarter, drilled 6 wells, and turned in line 9 wells, with the second rig repickup delayed until mid-October. CEO Mike Hollis acknowledged high debt, poor governance history, and past 'growth at all costs' mentality, outlining a long-term plan focused on debt reduction, free cash flow, and disciplined capital allocation, with scenarios tied to oil prices. The company also announced a share distribution plan over the next two years and expects 16-18 DUCs to support Q1-Q2 2026 production.

negative_highlights: Fintech non-GAAP gross margin fell to 68% from 97% due to revenue mix
R&D expenses increased year-over-year

positive_highlights: Q3 revenue beat guidance by 10%

Reaffirmed Q4 2025 and full-year 2026 revenue guidance
summary: Q3 FY2025 revenue from continuing operations was $4.4 million, up 37% year-over-year and 10% above guidance, driven by fintech, with payments revenue up 50% QoQ. Operating loss narrowed to $9.7 million from $10.3 million, and net loss improved 33% year-over-year to $0.26 per share. Management reaffirmed Q4 2025 revenue guidance of ~$6 million and full-year 2026 guidance of >=$32 million, and expects the Brands segment sale to reach a purchase agreement by end of Q4.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 33% year-over-year
Net loss of $19.6 million in quarter
Reducing headcount and moving away from legacy enzyme business
positive_highlights: Revenue expected to make or slightly exceed top end of 2025 guidance

11 revenue-bearing contracts in ECO Synthesis, up from 1 a year ago
summary: Codexis reported Q3 FY2025 total revenues of $8.6M, down from $12.8M in the prior year, with product gross margin improving to 64%. The company signed a supply assurance agreement with Merck and expects to make or slightly exceed the top end of 2025 guidance, with significant revenue recognition in Q4. They announced a strategic shift toward ECO Synthesis and ligase businesses, reducing headcount and small molecule biocatalysis sales efforts, extending cash runway through 2027. A new CEO transition was announced, with Alison Moore succeeding Stephen Dilly.

negative_highlights: Gain on sale margin guidance for Q4 is lower at 300-325 bps vs 339 bps in Q3
Origination volume decreased 3% sequentially to $6.5B

summary: In Q3 FY2025, loanDepot reported an adjusted net loss of $3 million, improved from a $16 million loss in Q2, with pull-through weighted rate lock volume of $7 billion (up 10% QoQ) and adjusted total revenue of $325 million (up from $292 million QoQ). Gain on sale margin was 339 bps, within guidance. For Q4, guidance calls for lock volume of $6-8 billion, origination volume of $6.5-8.5 billion, and gain on sale margin of 300-325 bps. Management highlighted leadership and technology changes and reiterated a focus on profitable market share growth, while noting capital structure review over the next 12-18 months.

negative_highlights: Q3 2025 product revenue only $0.9 million; net loss per share $0.09
EMA raised questions on TPOXX efficacy in mpox; CHMP decision pending
Government shutdown may delay CDC analysis for PEP program, affecting FDA submission timeline
positive_highlights: Product sales for 9 months outpaced prior year: $86 million vs $54 million
Cash balance strong at $172 million with no debt, more than 4x annual operating expense run rate
Management expects multiple international sales in 2026
summary: SIGA reported Q3 2025 product revenues of only $0.9 million, a quiet quarter after a strong Q2 with $79 million; nine-month product revenues were approximately $86 million versus $54 million in the prior year. The company noted $26 million of outstanding U.S. government orders for IV TPOXX expected for delivery in 2026. Management is actively engaged with the U.S. government on future procurement and remains encouraged despite the government shutdown, and expects multiple international sales in 2026. The EMA's CHMP will meet next week regarding the TPOXX referral, and management expressed confidence in their responses.

negative_highlights: Quarterly growth included a 600 basis point headwind from a lost advertiser
Political advertising created temporary distortion in reported growth
Majority of $250 million opportunity still undecided
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 7% YoY, above the midpoint of guidance

Flagship multiyear partnership with Molson Coors as advertising platform
summary: Viant reported record Q3 2025 results with revenue up 7% and contribution ex-TAC up 12%, both above the midpoint of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA reached $16 million, up 9% and above the high end of guidance. Excluding political advertising, revenue and contribution ex-TAC grew 19% and 22% respectively. The company highlighted a flagship multiyear partnership with Molson Coors and raised full-year guidance.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 4% YoY, with handheld revenue down 5%.
Approximately $4 million of Q4 revenue potentially impacted by government shutdown delays.
Gross margin decreased slightly to 53% due to product mix and unabsorbed precision machining costs.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.8 million was the lowest in company history, down 53% quarter-over-quarter.
Recurring revenue grew 10% YoY, and Explorer shipments set a record with 30% sequential growth.
Cash position strong at $112 million with no debt.
summary: 908 Devices reported Q3 2025 revenue of $14 million, down 4% YoY but up 8% sequentially, with gross margin at 53% on a GAAP basis and 58% on an adjusted basis. Recurring revenue grew 10% YoY to $4.8 million, representing 36% of total revenue. The adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $1.8 million, the lowest in company history, but management flagged an estimated $4 million of Q4 revenue at risk due to the U.S. government shutdown, while reaffirming full-year guidance. Explorer and Viper showed strong traction, with Explorer placements up 30% sequentially and Viper expected to ramp in 2026.

negative_highlights: CFO transition announced (Hadar leaving, incoming CFO Hod Cohen)

R&D grant expected to decline to ~$50k in Q4
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $18.4 million, up 16.2% year-over-year
Record non-GAAP operating income of $3.8 million (20.9% of revenue)
Positive cash flow of $5.1 million and record cash balance of $106.7 million
summary: RADCOM reported record Q3 2025 revenue of $18.4 million, up 16.2% year-over-year, with record non-GAAP operating income of $3.8 million (20.9% margin) and record non-GAAP EPS of $0.29. Cash flow from operations was $5.1 million, ending cash at $106.7 million. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance of 15-18% and targets double-digit growth for 2026, citing strong pipeline and new partnerships (NVIDIA, ServiceNow, 1Global) expected to contribute initial revenue in 2026.

Prelude Therapeutics reported strategic progress in Q3 FY2025, including an exclusive option agreement with Incyte for its JAK2V617F program, with $60 million upfront (including $25 million stock purchase) and potential $100 million option exercise payment plus milestones up to $775 million. Management highlighted two lead programs on track for IND filings in 2026: a JAK2V617F selective inhibitor (IND Q1 2026, Phase I in H1 2026) and a KAT6A selective degrader (IND mid-2026, Phase I in H2 2026). Preclinical data show differentiation over existing therapies, but no financial results (revenue, EPS) were provided, and clinical data readouts for KAT6 will likely not come until 2027. The tone is confident and forward-looking, emphasizing pipeline progress and business development.

negative_highlights: THP discontinued after failing to find strategic partner
Q4 growth expected to decelerate due to tough comparison and prior saline shortage benefits
Sequential EBITDA margin flat
positive_highlights: Net revenue grew 22% YoY to $26.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA improved by $2.3 million YoY
Distributor network expanded from 300 to 400+ in trailing twelve months
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q3 FY2025 surgical net revenue of $26.3 million, up 22% year-over-year, driven by soft tissue repair product sales up 24% to $23.4 million. Adjusted EBITDA improved by $2.3 million and operating cash flow was $2.2 million. The company announced discontinuation of Tissue Health Plus (THP) after failing to find a strategic partner, with expected cash costs of $5.5–$6.5 million in H2 2025 and no material cash spend after 2025. Management expects slower growth in Q4 2025 due to a tough comparison and one-time benefits from last year's saline shortage, but remains confident in the surgical business.

Major commercial vehicle OEM selected Innoviz for level 4 autonomous trucks
NRE payment plans raised above $110M for 2025-2027
summary: Innoviz reported Q3 2025 revenue of $15.3 million, with year-to-date revenue of $42.4 million, up 2.3x from the prior year. Management reaffirmed FY2025 revenue guidance of $50-60 million, more than double YoY, and raised NRE booking guidance to $30-60 million, already within range. The company announced a new level 4 autonomous trucking OEM win, ramped production at Fabrinet, and highlighted continued momentum in level 4 programs with VW/MOIA and non-automotive Innoviz Smart deployments. Innoviz Three was unveiled with a 60% smaller form factor and planned behind-windshield integration.

negative_highlights: U.S. revenue growth decelerated to just 1% YoY
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance cut to $89-$90 million
Operating leverage remains elusive with net loss of $14 million
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 75% from 74%
International revenue grew 15% YoY
Added 9 new U.S. centers in the quarter
summary: Pulmonx reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $21.5 million, up 5% YoY (4% constant currency), with U.S. revenue up only 1% and international up 15% (9% constant currency). Gross margin improved to 75% from 74%, but net loss remained at $14 million (EPS -$0.34) and adjusted EBITDA loss was $8.2 million. Management lowered full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $89-$90 million (from a prior range not in the transcript) and acknowledged slowing U.S. growth and lack of operating leverage. Newly returned CEO and CFO are conducting a bottom-up review to realign spending and extend cash runway, but provided no specifics.

negative_highlights: No financial results or guidance provided in the call
Phase III readouts not expected until mid-2026 and end of 2026
Ended formal engagement with Evercore, indicating no imminent strategic transaction
positive_highlights: Enrollment for CBEYOND on track to complete next month; top-line results mid-2026
Cash of $329.3 million provides runway through 2027
New dual mechanism of action for bemifovir may explain higher potency vs sofosbuvir
summary: Atea Pharmaceuticals reported no financials for the quarter; instead, the call focused on clinical progress. Enrollment for the Phase III HCV trial CBEYOND is on track to complete next month, with top-line results expected mid-2026; C FORWARD enrollment completes mid-2026 with results by end of 2026. New data highlighted a dual mechanism of action for bemifovir, no drug-drug interactions with PPIs, and positive resistance analysis. The company also announced expansion into hepatitis E with two preclinical candidates and maintained a strong cash position of $329.3 million, sufficient through 2027. The company ended its formal engagement with Evercore to focus on Phase III execution.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined $2.4 million year-over-year due to manufacturing inefficiencies and lower capacity utilization.
Gearing segment revenue down period-over-period due to lower deliveries and capacity utilization.
PRS softness continues, with customers citing oil prices as a restraint on capital.
positive_highlights: Orders increased 90% year-over-year to $44 million, the highest since 2022.
Industrial Solutions backlog hit a new record of $36 million for the fourth consecutive quarter.
Revenue guidance raised to $155–$160 million for fiscal 2025.
summary: Q3 FY2025 consolidated revenue rose 25% year-over-year to $44.2 million, beating prior guidance with orders up 90% year-over-year to nearly $44 million, the highest since 2022. Adjusted EBITDA fell by $2.4 million year-over-year to $3.4 million, impacted by manufacturing inefficiencies and lower gearing utilization. The company completed the sale of its Manitowoc industrial fabrication operations, boosting liquidity and reducing debt, and announced a $3 million share repurchase program. Management raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $155–$160 million (from $145–$155 million) while maintaining adjusted EBITDA guidance of $9–$10 million, and expects improved capacity utilization and operational leverage heading into 2026.

negative_highlights: NAV per share fell to $19.28 from $19.55 due to tariff-related losses
Two tariff-impacted investments drove $0.15 per share in unrealized losses
Fee income ran at about one-third of historical run rate; no Q4 supplemental dividend
positive_highlights: NII per share stable at $0.46 with 110% dividend coverage for Q3

Refinanced debt with over 90% maturing 2028 or later
summary: Q3 FY2025 NII was $0.46 per share, unchanged quarter-over-quarter, with 110% base dividend coverage. NAV fell to $19.28 from $19.55, driven by $0.15 per share in unrealized losses from two tariff-affected investments. Portfolio yield held at 10.4%, non-accruals improved to 1.6% from 2.4%, and management maintained the $0.42 dividend while flagging potential NII pressure from lower base rates. Fee income was about one-third of historical run rate, and no Q4 supplemental dividend was declared.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $8 million in Q3
Cash burn continues, though expected to decline
Reimbursement still mixed, with some denials
positive_highlights: Revenue up 87% YoY to $5.3M

CEO reaffirms 70% growth target, cites strong pipeline
summary: Profound Medical reported Q3 2025 revenue of $5.3 million, up 87% year-over-year, with recurring revenue of $4.1 million and capital equipment sales of $1.2 million. Gross margin improved to 74.3% from 63.1% a year ago, while net loss narrowed to $8 million from $9.4 million. The company announced full launch of its TULSA-AI Volume Reduction software at RSNA, increased installed base to 70 sites, and guided to sustained 70% growth. Management expressed confidence in achieving profitable growth, citing a pipeline of 93 new systems in late-stage sales processes.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined approximately $595,000 year-over-year
Revenue expected to be flat or down year-over-year for full year
Net loss of $965,000 in Q3 due to lower revenue
positive_highlights: Gross margin remained strong at 77% in Q3 2025
