Post-quarter $2.9 million net proceeds from warrant exercises strengthen cash position
summary: BIO-key reported Q3 2025 revenue of $1.55 million, down about $595,000 year-over-year primarily due to timing of large orders in Q3 2024. Gross margin remained strong at 77%, and operating expenses decreased 8% year-over-year. Net loss improved to $965,000 from $739,000 in Q3 2024 due to lower expenses. Management expects a strong Q4 and renewed subscription from a large banking customer in early 2026, with proceeds of $2.9 million raised post-quarter from warrant exercises strengthening liquidity.

negative_highlights: Q3 2025 loss from operations of $2.3 million with cash only $2.15 million at September 30
MoUs not yet converted to binding orders; timeline depends on future NRC approvals
No revenue reported in the quarter
positive_highlights: Completed business combination generating $109 million net proceeds, fully funding FOAK activities estimated at $17 million
Signed MoU for up to 100 Solo units representing $1.9 billion in potential revenue
NRC licensing fees reduced by 50% and accelerated dual-track licensing process in place
summary: Terra Innovatum reported its first earnings as a public company post business combination, with Q3 2025 loss from operations of $2.3 million and cash of $2.15 million at September 30. Management emphasized strong regulatory tailwinds, NRC licensing progress with FOAK approval expected in 2027 and commercial approval in 2028, and noted an MoU for up to 100 units worth $1.9 billion in potential revenue. They are fully funded with $109 million net proceeds to advance licensing and construction, and maintain confidence in converting pipeline to binding orders within 12 months.

negative_highlights: Voyage revenues fell 26% to $24.2 million due to 74 nonrevenue drydocking days
TCE rates dropped 40% compared to the same period in 2024
Cash balance decreased 48% to $6.6 million due to vessel purchase settlement
positive_highlights: Net income increased 281% to $5.26 million for 9M 2025 from a net loss in 2024
EBITDA rose 245% to $10 million for 9M 2025
Fleet is fully delevered; all CapEx obligations repaid without bank debt
summary: For the first 9 months of 2025, C3is reported net income of $5.26 million (up 281% YoY) and EBITDA of $10 million (up 245%), though voyage revenues fell 26% to $24.2 million due to 74 days of drydocking on its Aframax tanker, which also drove a 40% drop in TCE rates. The company settled the final $14.6 million balance on the Eco Spitfire in April 2025, leaving the fleet fully unencumbered with no bank debt. Management noted market uncertainty from geopolitics and tariffs but highlighted fleet quality and strategic relationships with repeat charters.

negative_highlights: Full-year sales were flat versus prior year
Tax expense of $25 million driven by $25.9 million deferred tax asset reserve
Management says it's too early to tell if market has turned
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 35.1%, up 1.2 points from prior year
New fishing products drove double-digit second-half growth
Operating loss improved to $16.2 million from prior year
summary: Johnson Outdoors reported full-year fiscal 2025 sales flat year-over-year, with an improved operating loss of $16.2 million versus the prior year. Gross margin improved 1.2 points to 35.1%, and operating expenses decreased 8%. Management highlighted strong demand for new fishing products driving double-digit second-half growth, but remained cautious on market recovery and faces headwinds from tariffs and a $25.9 million deferred tax asset reserve.

Application process failure and ACH fraud issues forced shutdown and reduced transactions
DraftKings and FanDuel have stopped credit card loads in some states
positive_highlights: No fraud has penetrated the app process in the last 60 days
BoltBetz licensing approvals and bank holding funds recognized by Gaming
Expect credit card volume to recover quickly once marketing resumes
summary: GBank reported Q4 2025 with credit card transaction volume declining to approximately $99 million from about $330 million in Q3, due to a deliberate pause in marketing and tighter fraud controls after an application process failure and ACH fraud concerns. Management emphasized investments in KYC, fraud prevention, and moving ACH in-house to rebuild a scalable foundation. They expect credit card volumes to recover quickly once marketing resumes, and anticipate a similar net interest margin for the coming year assuming a couple of rate cuts. SBA originations are expected to grow, with about 64% of originations sold, and noninterest expenses will rise with transaction volumes.

SBA gain on sale expected to drop to $19-20 million from $29.4 million in 2025
Credit issues in SBA portfolio may persist with more pain expected from late 2024/early 2025 originations
positive_highlights: Adjusted revenue up 21% year-over-year and adjusted pre-provision net revenue up 66%
Net interest margin expanded to 2.30% FTE, up 55 basis points year-over-year
BaaS deposits grew to $1.3 billion for 2025, more than tripling prior year
summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q4 2025 net income of $5.3 million or $0.60 per share (adjusted $0.64), with adjusted revenue up 21% year-over-year. Net interest margin expanded to 2.30% FTE, and full-year NII grew 30%. However, credit issues in SBA and franchise finance portfolios persist, with management guiding to a higher provision for 2026 and expecting credit to stabilize in the second half. Guidance for 2026 includes SBA production of ~$500 million and gain on sale revenue of $19-20 million (down from $29.4 million in 2025), while NIM is projected to rise to 2.75-2.80% by year-end. Loan growth expected 5-17% and deposit growth 8-10% for 2026.

Digital deposits declined less than 10% despite rate cuts

positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded to 3.28% from 2.90% year-over-year
Checking accounts grew 23%, noninterest-bearing deposits up to 16.3%
December core bank closed $75M commercial loans with $90M related deposits
summary: Primis Financial reported Q4 2025 earnings of $29.5 million or $1.20 per share, including a gain from a sale-leaseback transaction, with a nearly 3% ROA. Core run-rate earnings were about $8 million for 2025, an 80 basis point ROA, with margin expanding to 3.28% from 2.90% a year ago. The company grew checking accounts 23%, grew noninterest-bearing deposits to 16.3% of total deposits, and expects further margin expansion in 2026, targeting a 1% ROA. Management guided to core quarterly expenses of $23-24 million for 2026 and expressed confidence in achieving sustainable 1% ROA.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenues of $111.5 million down from $118.2 million year ago
Gross margin declined to 32.9% non-GAAP from 35.3% in prior year quarter
Full-year guidance unchanged; BEAD and new product contributions not yet material
positive_highlights: Highest second quarter bookings in the last ten years
Six-month revenues up 5.9% vs prior year; adjusted EBITDA up $13.2 million year-to-date
Initial purchase orders for PISA LTE 5G router and MDU solution with a US tier one provider
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $111.5 million, down from $118.2 million a year ago, but six-month revenues were $218.8 million, up 5.9% year over year. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.3 million (10.1% of revenues), non-GAAP EPS was $0.54, and operating cash flow was $23.9 million. Gross margins contracted year over year due to mix, but improved sequentially for the first half. Management kept full-year FY2026 guidance unchanged, noted highest Q2 bookings in ten years, and highlighted initial orders for its PISA cellular router and MDU solution, while keeping BEAD out of guidance.

negative_highlights: Tax expense of about $2 million from US valuation allowance
Operating expenses increased $2.1 million
Warranty expense decrease was less than a point of operating expense
positive_highlights: Revenue growth was double-digit, led by unit volumes
Gross margin improved 6.7 points to 36.6%
Pre-tax loss improved by $17.6 million year-over-year
summary: Q1 FY2026 pre-tax loss narrowed to $1.3 million from $18.9 million a year ago, with gross margin up 6.7 points to 36.6% on higher volumes, pricing, and cost savings. Revenue grew double-digit, driven by unit volumes and new products, with solid demand across Fishing, Jetboil, Old Town, and Scubapro's Hydros Pro 2. The company remains debt-free, reduced inventory by $17.7 million to $103.9 million, and continues its dividend, but tax rate will remain volatile due to US valuation allowance.

negative_highlights: 2025 was a challenging year; Q4 results do not reflect full potential
International retail, particularly EMEA, was softer than expected
Margins to be under pressure in the near term as production runs below wholesale
positive_highlights: North American dealer inventory declined 16% and globally down 17%, exceeding the 10% target
North American retail sales growth accelerated into December
Expects at least $150 million of annual run-rate savings impacting 2027 and beyond
summary: Q4 2025 was a challenging year with intentional wholesale reductions to address elevated dealer inventory, particularly touring in North America. Dealer inventory globally down 17% versus year-end 2024, exceeding the 10% target. Retail sales in North America were up year-over-year with December accelerating, but international retail especially EMEA was softer. Management sees 2026 as a transition year, expects margins under pressure, and announced at least $150 million of annual run-rate savings impacting 2027 and beyond. They are evaluating buyback timing and plan to share strategic details in May.

positive_highlights: Record annual revenue of $71.5M, up 17.2% YoY, above midpoint of 15%-18% guidance
Fourth-quarter operating margin of 23%, highest in eight years; gross margin 77.6% since 2018

Paying MAU declined 9% sequentially to 128,000 due to reduced UA spend, but ARPPU increased 7% and GMV grew. The jury awarded $420 million in damages against Papaya, with potential total award up to $1.2 billion, but collectability and timing remain uncertain. Guidance was not provided, and management's outlook is mixed: they expect PMAU to be flat to up with better unit economics, while RZR remains profitable for a third consecutive quarter.

Management highlighted broad-based strength, with high-growth businesses now nearly 50% of operating income and continued momentum expected.

summary: SSR Mining reported Q2 2026 production of 102,000 gold equivalent ounces at an AISC of $2,622/oz, with revenue of $443 million and adjusted EPS of $0.66. The company completed the sale of Çöpler and Hod Maden, exiting Türkiye, and ended the quarter with nearly $1.8 billion in cash and no debt. Management reiterated full-year production guidance but expects AISC to be at the upper end of guidance due to higher fuel costs and accelerated capital spend. Capital returns remain a focus, with $338 million returned via buybacks in Q2 and a reinstated dividend, implying a nearly 8% yield. The company plans to publish an updated Marigold technical report by year-end and is advancing growth projects across the portfolio.

summary: Otter Tail reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.66, down 10% year-over-year due to lower PVC pipe prices and higher corporate costs, but above expectations with strong manufacturing and plastics volumes. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.68-$6.08 from $5.22-$5.62, excluding the $103.5 million PVC antitrust settlement. Plastics segment adjusted results beat forecasts, with sales volumes up 15% and ASP decline moderating to 14%, though management expects continued pricing pressure into 2027. The company also secured route permits for two transmission projects and filed its 15-year IRP with Minnesota, reaffirming a 10% rate base growth CAGR.

summary: Enlight Renewable Energy reported Q2 2026 revenue and income of $210 million, up 55% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $160 million, up 67%. Net profit reached $31 million. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $790-820 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $565-585 million. Key milestones include financial close on the $2.6 billion CO Bar Complex, a PPA with Google for 200 MW in Oklahoma, and safe harboring 17.9 FGW of capacity.

summary: Sunoco LP reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $996 million (excluding $14 million of transaction expenses), up sharply year-over-year, with Fuel Distribution EBITDA of $516 million, Pipeline Systems of $190 million, Terminals of $115 million, and Refinery of $175 million. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $3.5-3.7 billion from $3.1-3.3 billion, citing strength across all segments and contributions from recent acquisitions. Distributable Cash Flow as adjusted was $608 million, with a distribution increase of 1.25% sequentially and over 10% year-over-year. Management expressed confidence in continued growth, noting a 2.1x coverage ratio and leverage of approximately 3.7x, below the 4x target.

Same unit pricing rose 4% on strong RCM collections, payer mix, and acuity, partially offset by volumes down 2% (NICU days down 3%). Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $280-$300 million and continues share buybacks.

summary: MPLX reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 billion, up 5% year-over-year, overcoming the Rockies divestiture. The company highlighted strong utilization (Delaware Basin 86%, Marcellus 96%) and raised its 2026 capital outlook by $500 million to $2.9 billion, primarily pulling forward Gulf Coast fractionation spend. Management reiterated mid-single-digit EBITDA growth for 2026 and 2027, with sequential growth expected in Q3 and Q4, and maintained 12.5% distribution growth guidance for 2026 and 2027, along with a 1.3x coverage target.

summary: Jackson Financial reported record Q2 2026 adjusted operating EPS of $7.30, with ex-notables EPS of $7.68, up 55% year-over-year. Retail annuity sales rose 34% to about $6 billion, with record RILA sales of $2.3 billion. First-half free cash flow reached $575 million (up 14% YoY) and capital returned to shareholders was $547 million. Management reaffirmed full-year free capital generation target of $1.2 billion and capital return target of $900 million to $1.1 billion, and announced CEO transition.

summary: Pinnacle West reported Q2 2026 EPS of $1.43, down $0.15 YoY, with strong customer and sales growth (2.1% customer growth, 9.6% weather-normalized sales growth) partially offset by higher interest, depreciation, and lower transmission revenue. Management reiterated full-year guidance of $4.55-$4.75, expecting to finish at the top end, and highlighted major growth drivers including TSMC's additional $100 billion investment and a new $500 million ATM program. The company is progressing through its rate case and expects a final commission decision before year-end.

summary: Crexendo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $24.6 million, up 49% year-over-year, beating top-line expectations, with GAAP net income of $1.1 million ($0.03 per share) in line with expectations and non-GAAP net income of $4.1 million ($0.12 per share), beating expectations by 200 basis points. Adjusted EBITDA of $4.1 million was up 46% year-over-year, and margins expanded across all segments, with consolidated gross margin up 500 basis points sequentially to 66%. The company added six new NetSapiens logos in the quarter (11 year-to-date vs. 2 last year), ESI acquisition contributed $6.9 million in revenue, and remaining performance obligation increased 97% to $139 million. Management maintained double-digit organic growth guidance for the year and expects AI-related revenue to become meaningful in 2027.

Base44 gross margin improved from near 0% to approximately 60% in the second half, driven by the new proprietary LLM Base1, but the company plans to reinvest these savings into sales and marketing, keeping guidance unchanged. Management expressed confidence in AI strategy and product leadership, though they noted some FX headwinds and elevated S&M expenses.

Adjusted EPS was $3.38, up 5% constant currency, with a reduced FX tailwind; 50,000 restaurants target pushed to 2028. Management is acting to simplify ops and reallocate marketing.

AI adoption surged 121% YoY, AI Studio gained over 200 customers and 2,900 agents within 3.5 months of launch, and the company raised its fiscal year revenue outlook. Management emphasized ongoing momentum, multi-product adoption, and a partner-first strategy while acknowledging near-term volatility.

summary: Compass reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.3 billion, up 14% year-over-year on a pro forma basis, and record adjusted EBITDA of $363 million, both above guidance. The company raised its year-one cost synergies target to $330 million from $300 million, achieved five months ahead of schedule, and increased 2026 in-year net synergies to $220 million. Brokerage GTV grew about 16% year-over-year versus market up 6%, an acceleration in outperformance from Q1, and net debt/EBITDA fell to 3.3x from 4.2x sequentially.

summary: Gilead reported strong Q2 2026 results with base business sales up 10% YoY, driven by HIV, Trodelvy, and Livdelzi. HIV sales grew 12% YoY, with PrEP sales doubling to exceed $1 billion quarterly for the first time. The company raised full-year HIV growth guidance to 9%-10% from 8%, citing strong Biktarvy and PrEP momentum. Trodelvy sales were up 26% YoY on new first-line approvals, while cell therapy declined 14% YoY amid competition. Management highlighted upcoming launches for BIC/LEN and anito-cel before year-end.

The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance, with adjusted operating income midpoint of $2.2 billion and adjusted EPS midpoint of $14.65. Management highlighted accelerating volume growth and progress on middle molecule clearance, but noted revenue per treatment declined sequentially and policy rate updates track below cost trends.

summary: MNTN reported Q2 2026 revenue of $82.5 million, up 21% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $21.5 million, up 48%, both at the high end of guidance. Gross margins expanded 350 basis points to 80%, and active PTV customers grew 40% year-over-year to 4,225. Management guided Q3 revenue to $86-$89 million (25% growth at midpoint) and reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $347-$357 million. They announced a $100 million stock repurchase program and highlighted strong adoption of MNTN Express and QuickFrame AI, expecting bigger contributions in 2027.

summary: Xometry reported record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue up 41% YoY to $229 million, marketplace revenue accelerating to 45% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA improving to $14.1 million. Active buyers grew 20% YoY to over 89,000, with a record net addition of 175 accounts spending over $50,000. Management raised second-half guidance again, citing strong Q3 momentum and confidence in AI-driven growth and operating leverage. Gross margin is expected to expand toward the 35-40% target range over time, with marketplace gross margin up about 100 basis points in the first half.

summary: Urban One reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net revenues of $85.8 million, down 6.4% year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA fell 16% to $11.7 million, with declines across all segments. Management lowered full-year guidance to mid-50s from 60, citing a weak first half, though they expect political spending in Q3 to help. The company repurchased $23.5 million of debt at a discount, closed the Dallas acquisition, and recognized $14.1 million in non-cash impairment charges at Reach Media.
